finding.claim: Broken authorization: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the boolean result instead of calling require_edit()/abort(403). Any authenticated user can overwrite the body of any document they neither own nor edit.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (g.user) sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with a JSON body, using a doc_id they have no rights to
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to the document body)

trace.note: doc fetched by attacker-supplied doc_id with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) return value ignored, so no abort occurs

finding.guards_checked: can_edit is called but never enforced. require_edit (docs.py:11) is used correctly in update_title (line 27) but not here. No before_request/auth decorator or other check is visible in the file. g.user is never set in this file, so authentication is assumed to come from elsewhere. If no auth runs, the endpoint is also open to unauthenticated callers.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at docs.py:19; require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which aborts with 403, is used only in update_title (line 27). No before_request or decorator exists in the file.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 discards the boolean from can_edit(g.user, doc), so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller who reaches the route, unlike update_title at docs.py:27, which enforces require_edit.

verdict_facts.guard_found: can_edit (docs.py:7) returns a bool but its result is discarded at line 19; require_edit (docs.py:11), which aborts with 403, is used only in update_title (line 27). No decorator or before_request check exists in this file.
verdict_facts.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement and ignores the result, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller who supplies a valid doc_id.
